original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
A 42-year-old fled from police before being involved in a two-vehicle crash in Sans Souci, police say

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three people have died in a crash in Sydney after a man fled police who had been attempting to carry out a welfare check.

A 42-year-old man fled in a white Audi after officers were called to a welfare check at a property in Gymea Bay, southern Sydney, at 12.25am on Saturday.

Shortly afterwards, police received reports that an Audi had rolled over a concrete barrier and landed on a blue Toyota sedan at Sans Souci, about 7km away.

The man died at the scene, as did the driver and passenger of the Toyota, who are yet to be formally identified.

Superintendent Graham Hibbs said police had been called to do a welfare check before the accident.

“All I can really say at this stage is we were called for a concern for welfare, a mental health incident,” he said. “And that’s all the detail I can provide at this stage.”

Police were not able to speak with the man before he fled. Officers believed the Audi was travelling at “considerable speed” when the crash occurred, Hibbs said.

“It was a horrific scene. We really feel for the families of all three persons and their loved ones,” he said.

“I don’t think there were many cars on the road at that time.”

Between 20 and 40 bystanders attempted to assist when one of the cars caught fire.

“We really feel for the families of all three persons who were involved in this incident and their loved ones,” he said.

A crime scene has been established, and investigations are continuing into the crash circumstances, with drugs and alcohol a line of inquiry.

It has been a deadly 24 hours on Australian roads after a 25-year-old woman and an infant died in a two-car crash near a popular holiday spot in Queensland.

In a separate crash in Queensland, two girls, aged 13 and 14, suffered serious injuries after they were hit by a car while on a footpath in South Mackay.

---

[Lähde: ABC (Australian Broadcasting Corporation)]
Three people have died in a road crash in Sans Souci in Sydney's south. (ABC News)

Three people have died in a car crash in Sydney's south, with police attempting to conduct a welfare check at one of the victim's homes minutes before the incident.

Police attended a home on Second Avenue, Gymea Bay at 12:25am on Saturday following reports of a concern for welfare related to a mental health incident.

A 42-year-old man left the home in a white Audi before officers could speak to him.

Shortly after at 12:30am, emergency services were called to Rocky Point Road at San Souci after reports of a two-car crash.

Police found that the same white Audi had rolled over a concrete barrier before landing on a blue Toyota sedan.

Police say the Audi was travelling at "considerable speed". (ABC News)

The 42-year-old Audi driver died at the scene, as did the driver and passenger of the Toyota.

Investigators have yet to formally identify the occupants of the Toyota.

Superintendent Graham Hibbs said officers believed the Audi was travelling at "considerable speed" when the crash occurred.

Police say bystanders attempted to assist at the scene. (ABC News: Sean Tarek Goodwin)

"We really feel for the families of all three persons who were involved in this incident and their loved ones," he said.

He said between 20 and 40 bystanders attempted to assist when one of the cars caught fire.

Superintendent Hibbs said first responders would have been met with a "horrific scene".

A crime scene has been established and an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash is underway.

Rocky Point Road remains closed between Sans Souci and Taren Point, with motorists advised to avoid the area.

A report will be prepared for the coroner.

---

[Lähde: 7NEWS Australia]
Three people have died in a “horrific and tragic” head-on collision that has left two vehicles mangled.

Emergency services were called to Rocky Point Rd in San Souci, South Sydney, to reports of a two car crash about 12.30am on Saturday.

WATCH THE VIDEO ABOVE: Three killed in horrific Sydney collision

Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today

A white Audi had landed on its roof following the collision, while the top of a blue Camry was found with its roof smashed in.

About 12.25am, police officers attended a home on Second Ave in Gymea, about 8km south of the crash scene, to speak to a 42-year-old man regarding reports of a mental health incident.

As police arrived, however, the man left the scene in a white Audi before police could speak to him.

Soon after, police were called to the crash site.

The 42-year-old male driver of the Audi and both the male driver and passenger of the Camry were killed in the crash.

7NEWS understands the Audi was launched into the air after crashing into a dividing barrier and landing on top of the Camry.

“It was a horrific scene,” Detective Acting Superintendent Graham Hibbs said.

“The circumstances of what has occurred last night, from what I understand, are horrific and tragic.

“We really feel for the families of all three persons who were involved in this incident and their loved ones.”

Hibbs said the Camry had been “extremely unlucky” to be involved in the incident.

“I don’t think there were many cars on the road at that time,” he said.

Up to 40 locals raced to the scene soon after the crash to try to help the victims.

“Some of the bystanders rushed over to offer what minimal assistance they could offer in the circumstances,” Hibbs said.

“The engine bay of one of the vehicles had caught alight and they are assisted with putting that out.“

“It was obviously quite a high-impact crash, it was obviously quite a distressing scene for those people.

“It wouldn’t be nice for any person to see that scene that occurred this morning.”

Rocky Point Rd has been shut in both directions as the Crash Investigation Unit assists police with inquiries into the crash.

Anyone with information, including CCTV, dashcam or mobile phone footage, has been urged to contact Crime Stopper...

payload.title: Kolme kuoli kolarissa Sydneyn eteläosassa poliisin hyvinvointitarkastuksen jälkeen
payload.summary: Kolme ihmistä on kuollut kahden auton kolarissa Sans Soucissa Sydneyn eteläosassa sen jälkeen, kun poliisi oli mennyt tarkistamaan 42-vuotiaan miehen vointia Gymea Bayssa.
payload.content:
Kolme ihmistä on kuollut kahden auton kolarissa Sans Soucissa Sydneyn eteläosassa varhain lauantaina. Poliisin mukaan tapaus alkoi, kun viranomaiset menivät Gymea Bayssa sijaitsevaan asuntoon tekemään hyvinvointitarkastusta mielenterveyteen liittyneen ilmoituksen vuoksi. Ennen kuin poliisit ehtivät puhua 42-vuotiaan miehen kanssa, hän poistui paikalta valkoisella Audilla.

## Poliisi oli matkalla hyvinvointitarkastukseen

Poliisi sai ilmoituksen Gymea Bayssa sijaitsevaan osoitteeseen lauantaina noin kello 0.25 paikallista aikaa. Kyse oli viranomaisten mukaan huolesta henkilön hyvinvoinnista ja mielenterveyteen liittyneestä tilanteesta.

Paikalle saapuneet poliisit eivät ehtineet keskustella 42-vuotiaan miehen kanssa, sillä hän lähti asunnolta valkoisella Audilla. Lyhyen ajan kuluttua hätäkeskukseen tuli ilmoitus vakavasta liikenneonnettomuudesta Sans Soucissa, noin seitsemän tai kahdeksan kilometrin päässä alkuperäisestä tapahtumapaikasta.

## Auto päätyi toisen ajoneuvon päälle

Onnettomuus tapahtui Rocky Point Roadilla noin kello 0.30. Poliisin mukaan valkoinen Audi oli ylittänyt tai vierinyt betonisen esteen yli ja päätynyt sinisen Toyota-sedanin päälle. Viranomaiset ovat kuvailleet Audin liikkuneen huomattavalla nopeudella ennen törmäystä.

Audiin liittynyt 42-vuotias mies kuoli tapahtumapaikalla. Myös Toyotan kuljettaja ja matkustaja menehtyivät onnettomuudessa. Heitä ei ollut vielä lähdetietojen mukaan virallisesti tunnistettu.

Pelastusviranomaiset hälytettiin paikalle kahden auton kolarin vuoksi. Lähteiden kuvaukset ajoneuvoista kertovat voimakkaasta törmäyksestä: Audi oli päätynyt katolleen ja toinen auto oli vaurioitunut pahoin.

## Tapahtumien kulkua selvitetään

Poliisi selvittää nyt, mitä tapahtui niiden minuuttien aikana, jotka seurasivat hyvinvointitarkastusta Gymea Bayssa. Keskeistä tutkinnassa on Audin kulkureitti ja nopeus ennen törmäystä sekä se, miten auto päätyi vastaantulevan tai toisen ajoneuvon päälle Sans Soucissa.

Viranomaiset eivät ole kertoneet julkisuuteen kaikkia uhrien henkilötietoja. Tapauksen taustalla ollut hyvinvointitarkastus ei lähdetietojen perusteella tarkoita, että kolariin liittyvien muiden henkilöiden toiminnasta olisi esitetty epäilyjä.
summary_bullets: Kolme ihmistä kuoli kahden auton kolarissa Sans Soucissa Sydneyn eteläosassa.
Tapaus alkoi poliisin hyvinvointitarkastuksesta Gymea Bayssa noin kello 0.25 paikallista aikaa.
Poliisin mukaan 42-vuotias mies poistui paikalta valkoisella Audilla ennen kuin viranomaiset ehtivät puhua hänen kanssaan.
Audi päätyi hetkeä myöhemmin sinisen Toyota-sedanin päälle Rocky Point Roadilla.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu usean lähteen yhteneviin tietoihin kuolonuhreista, ajankohdasta, paikasta ja poliisin hyvinvointitarkastuksesta. Uhrien henkilöllisyyksiä ja tutkinnan tarkempia johtopäätöksiä ei ole lisätty, koska niitä ei ollut paketissa vahvistettu.

## Tapahtumien kulkua selvitetään

Poliisi selvittää nyt, mitä tapahtui niiden minuuttien aikana, jotka seurasivat hyvinvointitarkastusta Gymea Bayssa. Keskeistä tutkinnassa on Audin kulkureitti ja nopeus ennen törmäystä sekä se, miten auto päätyi vastaantulevan tai toisen ajoneuvon päälle Sans Soucissa.

Viranomaiset eivät ole kertoneet julkisuuteen kaikkia uhrien henkilötietoja. Tapauksen taustalla ollut hyvinvointitarkastus ei lähdetietojen perusteella tarkoita, että kolariin liittyvien muiden henkilöiden toiminnasta olisi esitetty epäilyjä.

(ABC News) Three people have died in a car crash in Sydney's south, with police attempting to conduct a welfare check at one of the victim's homes minutes before the incident. Police attended a home on Second Avenue, Gymea Bay at 12:25am on Saturday following reports of a concern for welfare related to a mental health incident. A 42-year-old man left the home in a white Audi before officers could speak to him. Shortly after at 12:30am, emergency services were called to Rocky Point Road at San Souci after reports of a two-car crash. Police found that the same white Audi had rolled over a concrete barrier before landing on a blue Toyota sedan. Police say the Audi was travelling at "considerable speed". (ABC News)
